skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.description: Run structured code reviews that check security, code quality, performance, tests, and documentation using guidance plus optional local analysis tools.
skill.summary: Reviews code changes for security, quality, performance, testing, and documentation concerns.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from documentation that intentionally shows vulnerable and safe code examples for reviewer education. The helper script uses fixed local tools with argument lists rather than shell execution, but its report output can overwrite a user-selected local file.

remediation.issue: Report output path can overwrite local files.
remediation.suggestion: Before writing --output, refuse directories, warn on existing files, or require an explicit overwrite flag.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples trigger many high-risk static patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Label vulnerable examples clearly and keep them in documentation-only files so users do not copy them into production code.

content.user_title: Review Code for Security and Quality
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security flaws, performance regressions, and weak tests. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured review workflow with checklists and optional helper analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviews through security, quality, performance, testing, and documentation phases.
Provides checklists for pull requests, architecture checks, and language-specific review items.
Includes examples of common vulnerabilities and safer alternatives for review reference.
Can run a local Python helper for Bandit, Radon, Pylint, and Safety when those tools are installed.
Generates Markdown, text, or JSON-style review summaries from helper results.
limitations: The helper script focuses on Python tooling and does not deeply analyze every language.
External tools such as Bandit, Radon, Pylint, and Safety must be installed separately.
Findings require human review because automated scanners can miss context or report false positives.
The skill does not replace project-specific coding standards or threat modeling.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request before merge
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to inspect changed files for correctness, security, test coverage, and documentation gaps.

use_cases.title: Audit a codebase for common security issues
use_cases.description: Use the security patterns and checklist to look for injection, access control, secrets, XSS, deserialization, and cryptography problems.

use_cases.title: Improve team review consistency
use_cases.description: Use the checklist and feedback patterns to standardize review expectations across projects and reviewers.

prompt_templates.title: Basic pull request review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for correctness, security, tests, and documentation. Focus on high-impact issues and explain each finding clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Security-focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a security-focused review of this code. Look for injection, access control, secrets, unsafe deserialization, weak cryptography, and data exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Performance and maintainability review
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a service or library change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code for performance bottlenecks, excessive complexity, resource leaks, and maintainability risks. Prioritize issues that affect production behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Comprehensive release readiness review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a comprehensive review across security, correctness, performance, tests, dependencies, and documentation. Separate blocking issues from suggestions.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that adds a new API endpoint.
output: Blocking: authorization is missing on the new endpoint.
High: input validation does not reject invalid IDs.
Suggestion: add a regression test for unauthorized access.

output_examples.input: Check a Python module before release.
output: Security scan completed with two findings to verify.
Complexity review found one function above the target threshold.
Documentation should describe the new configuration option.

output_examples.output: The review highlights duplicated validation logic, one risky behavior change, and missing tests for the error path.

best_practices: Run project tests and linters before asking for a review so the review can focus on logic and risk.
Provide the change intent and affected files so findings can be evaluated against the real goal.
Treat automated tool results as signals and verify each finding against code context.
anti_patterns: Do not use the checklist as a substitute for reading the changed code carefully.
Do not accept every scanner result without checking whether it is reachable or relevant.
Do not focus on style issues while ignoring security, correctness, or test gaps.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically fix code?
faq.answer: No. It guides review and can generate reports. Any changes should be made deliberately by the user or agent.

faq.question: Which tools can it use?
faq.answer: The helper script can call Bandit, Radon, Pylint, and Safety when they are installed locally.

faq.question: Is it only for Python projects?
faq.answer: No. The review guidance covers several languages, but the included helper script is Python-centered.

faq.question: Can it review security issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes security checklists and examples for injection, secrets, access control, XSS, deserialization, and cryptography.

faq.question: Can it replace a human reviewer?
faq.answer: No. It improves coverage and consistency, but a human should verify findings and business logic.

faq.question: Does it send code to external services?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the skill files. The helper script runs local command-line tools.
